title: Gateways are All You Need — Karan Sampath, Anthropic
talk_summary: An Anthropic forward-deployed engineer argues that enterprises adopting MCP servers hit a wall on observability, access control, and security, and that a centralized MCP gateway (auth, RBAC, proxy/routing, tunnel, sub-registry, CLI) is the one-time investment that unblocks decentralized server development. The gateway becomes the single root of trust, letting teams build servers without repeated security reviews and decoupling the agent harness from the data/tool layer.

takeaways.technique: Centralized tool/MCP gateway as single root of trust
takeaways.what_they_do: Put one gateway between all clients and all MCP servers so auth, access control, routing, tunneling, and a sub-registry live in one place; individual servers only implement business logic.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the goal for a secure this for any security team is to is to bless one platform

takeaways.what_they_do: Encode company operating procedures and allowed tool shapes as gateway primitives so every new server/tool automatically conforms instead of relying on repeated manual security review.
takeaways.evidence_quote: A gateway is a way of encoding that. A gateway is a way of you being like, "These are my standard procedures"

takeaways.technique: Decouple agent harness from data/tool layer
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep the gateway invariant while swapping agent harnesses (managed vs in-house SDK) behind it, so agent design choices don't couple to data/tool structure.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we want to separate the agent harness from where your data lives

takeaways.technique: Gateway CLI for self-service server creation
takeaways.what_they_do: Provide a CLI the gateway exposes so any team (or their coding agent) can scaffold a new MCP server that auto-integrates auth, routing, and registry.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the gateway has a quick and easy CLI that not you, not that team, but but the agent that team is using

takeaways.technique: Gateway observability of tool usage and definitions
takeaways.what_they_do: Log which tools/MCPs are used and how they're defined, to find load-bearing tools and adapt them as the protocol/agents evolve.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you not only want usage metrics to reflect what MCPs are being used, but you also kind of want to know how how are your tools being defined
